key_insight: The paper finds that reinforcement learning post-training for LLMs does not need to update every transformer layer. Training just a single well-chosen layer can match the performance of full-parameter RL training in many cases.
problem_solved: It addresses the inefficiency and lack of understanding in standard RL post-training, where all model parameters are updated uniformly even though not every layer may contribute equally to adaptation.
method: Conduct a systematic layer-wise study of RL training across transformer layers.
Compare performance when updating individual layers versus training all parameters.
Identify whether one layer can capture most of the RL adaptation signal and match full-model gains.
impact: This could dramatically reduce the cost, memory use, and complexity of RL fine-tuning for large language models. For practitioners, it suggests a more targeted and efficient path to post-training without sacrificing performance.
visual_elements: Transformer stack diagram highlighting a single trained layer versus all layers
Performance comparison bar chart: single-layer RL vs full-parameter RL
Layer-wise heatmap showing which layers benefit most from RL updates
Efficiency icon set showing reduced compute, memory, and training time
paper_title: Is One Layer Enough? Training A Single Transformer Layer Can Match Full-Parameter RL Training
paper_authors: Zijian Zhang, Rizhen Hu, Athanasios Glentis, Dawei Li, Chung-Yiu Yau
